rules.name: Repeated authentication failures
rules.summary: At least five authentication failures for the same account, host, and source IP occurred within ten minutes.
data_sources: Authentication logs normalized to auth_failure with timestamp, host, user, and source_ip.
recommended_actions: Review the authentication timeline and confirm whether the source is expected.
Check for a successful login from the same source after the failures.

rules.name: Authentication failures followed by success
rules.summary: A successful authentication followed failures for the same account, host, and source IP within fifteen minutes; validate whether this represents suspected credential guessing or an expected recovery.
data_sources: Authentication logs normalized to auth_failure and auth_success with timestamp, host, user, and source_ip.
recommended_actions: Validate the login with the account owner through an approved channel.
Review subsequent activity for the account and preserve relevant logs.

rules.name: PowerShell execution flagged by endpoint telemetry
rules.summary: Endpoint telemetry flagged a PowerShell execution for review; the ATT&CK mapping describes the observed interpreter, not malicious intent by itself.
data_sources: Endpoint process telemetry with interpreter, process ancestry, user, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Review process ancestry, user context, script block or command-line telemetry, and the related host timeline.
Do not isolate or stop a process until the alert is validated.

rules.name: Privileged group membership changed

attack.technique_name: Account Manipulation: Additional Local or Domain Groups

rules.summary: A privileged local or domain group membership change was recorded; validate the account, group, and approval context.
data_sources: Identity or operating-system audit events for privileged group membership changes, including actor, target account, group, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Confirm the change was approved and identify the initiating account.
Review nearby authentication and process events on the affected host.

rules.name: Password-spray pattern across distinct accounts
rules.summary: Authentication failures affected five or more distinct accounts on the same host from one source IP within ten minutes, a password-spraying indicator that requires investigation.
data_sources: Authentication logs with normalized user, host, source_ip, and timestamp; distinct user values are required.
recommended_actions: Compare the targeted account set and source against approved identity and network activity.
Review MFA, conditional-access, and account-lockout outcomes for the affected users.

rules.name: New scheduled task created
rules.summary: A scheduled task creation event was reported; check the task action, trigger, creator, and execution context.
data_sources: Windows Task Scheduler or endpoint audit telemetry with task name, action, creator, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Compare the task definition and binary path with the approved software baseline.
Confirm the task creator and execution account with the system owner.

rules.name: Registry Run key modified

attack.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

rules.summary: A Windows Run or RunOnce autostart location changed; validate the new value and its initiating process.
data_sources: Windows Registry auditing for Run/RunOnce and Startup Folder changes, with value, process, user, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Inspect the changed value and referenced file using approved endpoint tooling.
Check whether the change aligns with a documented installation or update.

rules.name: Suspicious LSASS memory access signal
rules.summary: Endpoint telemetry flagged an unusual process access to LSASS memory, which may expose credential material.
data_sources: Endpoint process-access telemetry identifying the source process, target process, user, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Review process signer, ancestry, access rights, and nearby authentication events.
Follow the organization's credential-exposure procedure if the activity is confirmed.

rules.name: Windows Event Log configuration changed

attack.technique_name: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log

rules.summary: Windows Event Log service or audit-policy telemetry reported a configuration change that may reduce visibility.
data_sources: Windows service-control, audit-policy, and Event Log configuration telemetry with actor, setting, host, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Confirm the change against approved maintenance and audit-policy records.
Check whether other event channels or security sensors stopped reporting at the same time.

rules.name: Network service probing across multiple destinations
rules.summary: A sensor reported probes to three or more distinct destination addresses from one host and source within five minutes.
data_sources: Network flow, firewall, or endpoint socket telemetry with source host, destination IP, timestamp, and optional destination port.
recommended_actions: Compare the source host and destination set with approved inventory, vulnerability scanning, and management tools.
Review process or user context associated with the probes.

rules.name: Remote SSH session observed
rules.summary: An SSH session was reported by normalized telemetry; confirm whether the source, destination, and account are expected.
data_sources: SSH authentication and session logs with user, source_ip, destination host, outcome, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Validate the account, source address, and destination against approved administration paths.
Correlate the session with nearby authentication and process events on the destination.

rules.name: Repeated DNS tunneling or beaconing signal
rules.summary: DNS analytics raised three or more tunneling or beaconing signals from the same host and source in ten minutes.
data_sources: DNS resolver or network analytics with client host, queried domain, record type, query timing, and anomaly signal.
recommended_actions: Review queried domains, record types, query cadence, and the process responsible for the DNS traffic.
Compare the activity with approved DNS tooling and resolver policy.

rules.name: Sensitive file access followed by unusual outbound transfer
rules.summary: Sensitive-file access was followed by an outbound transfer anomaly for the same host and user within fifteen minutes; validate the destination and process context.
data_sources: File-access auditing plus network-flow or proxy telemetry linking host/user activity to outbound destination and transfer volume.
recommended_actions: Preserve the file-access and network-flow evidence and validate the destination against approved services.
Review the process responsible for the transfer and follow the organization's data-handling escalation path.

rules.name: Email attachment followed by suspicious child process
rules.summary: An email attachment interaction was followed by suspicious child-process telemetry for the same user and host within fifteen minutes.
data_sources: Email security metadata and endpoint process-creation telemetry correlated by user, host, attachment, parent process, and timestamp.
recommended_actions: Review the message, attachment hash, process ancestry, and endpoint verdicts.
Check for subsequent persistence, credential-access, and outbound-network activity.
